blocks.text: The exercise creates two independent copies of the input before demonstrating two indexing operations. That first step is important: it isolates the examples and leaves the caller’s input unchanged. Both branches select positions zero, two, and four. Their selected values initially look identical, but the references to storage are different.
Demonstrate views versus copies: return two copies of the input, modifying every second element through a slice in one and through fancy indexing in the other. Use -1 as the replacement.

An ndarray combines stored values with metadata such as shape and strides. A view has its own metadata but refers to an existing buffer. A copy has separate data storage. Equal values therefore do not prove that two arrays share memory.

In the slice branch, a[::2] creates a view. Its stride skips one original element each time. When view[:] is assigned −1, those writes reach positions zero, two, and four in a. The view is not a list of detached values. Trace the arrows in the diagram to see why the returned a contains alternating replacements.

blocks.text: Connect the picture to the mathematics

blocks.caption: The base is the starting memory location. The stride is the byte distance between consecutive entries of a one-dimensional view.

blocks.text: In the integer-array branch, b[np.arange(0,len(b),2)] performs advanced indexing and returns copied values. Writing into this temporary array changes only the temporary buffer. The returned b therefore retains all original values. This distinction is about storing the indexed result and then mutating it. Direct assignment b[index_array] = value follows NumPy’s assignment rules and does modify b.

The memory relationship can matter more than the numerical result. A helper that unexpectedly mutates a view can alter an input used later in training. An unnecessary copy can consume substantial memory. Check np.shares_memory for overlap when you need evidence, and distinguish basic slicing from advanced indexing. Also avoid treating every reshape as a guaranteed view: the answer depends on layout and whether a copy is required.
blocks.title: The boundary of this implementation

notes.text: Basic slicing creates the alias that later writes use.
Advanced integer indexing creates independent data for this temporary result.
